paper.title: Adaptive Incentive Design in Dynamic Principal-Agent Problem via Kernelized Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic principal-agent problem with stochastic agent utility (kernelized bandit over contract space [0,1]^m with heteroscedastic noise)
unmapped: Contract space X=[0,1]^m (paper's m = dimension = number of outcomes)
Reward function lies in RKHS of the arcsin (neural network) kernel with known RKHS norm bound B
Heteroscedastic noise whose variance lies in an RKHS (Gaussian kernel) with known norm bound B_v; noise bounded by sqrt(chi_u)
Sample-variance noise eta is rho_eta(x)-sub-Gaussian with known rho_eta
Learner takes ell>1 repeated samples per chosen contract
Agent has finite action set, hidden actions; agent utility has stochastic perturbation <w, delta(a)> with absolutely continuous w
settings.definition_quote: \Tilde{R}_T= T\Tilde{U}^{\mathrm{P}*} - \sum_{t=1}^T \Tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}(x_t), where \Tilde{U}^{\mathrm{P}*}= \max_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \:\: \Tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}(x). ... \tilde{y}_t= \tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}(x_t) + \tilde{\varepsilon}(x_t), where \tilde{\varepsilon}(x_t) is assumed to be a zero-mean heteroscedastic noise

algorithms.name: Heteroscedastic GP-UCB (with Neural Network / arcsin kernel)
requires_knowledge_of: B_v (RKHS norm bound of noise variance)

conditions: \tilde U^{PA} in RKHS H_k of the arcsin kernel with ||.||_{H_k} <= B
Assumption 4.2: noise variance in RKHS of kernel kappa^v with norm <= B_v
Assumption 4.3: variance-estimate noise eta is rho_eta-sub-Gaussian with known rho_eta, independent in time
contract space [0,1]^m; d here denotes the paper's m
tuning: beta_t as in eq. (beta_t) with confidence delta

source.label: main_theorem
source.quote: Consider $\tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}} \in \mathcal{H}_k$ with bounded RKHS-norm (i.e., $\|\tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}\|_{\mathcal{H}_k} \le B$) and sampling model in \eqref{feedback_eq} with unknown variance ... that satisfies Assumptions~\ref{var_proxy_assumption} and~\ref{noise_assumption}. Let $\{x_t\}_{t=1}^{T}$ denote the set of actions chosen by Algorithm~\ref{algo}. Setting $\lambda=1$ in \eqref{beta_t}, the cumulative regret $\Tilde{R}_T$ ... is bounded as $\mathbb{P}\left[\Tilde{R}_T \leq \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{T}(\log T)^{m+1}\right)\right] \geq 1 - \delta$

results.notes: Paper's m is the dimension of the contract space, mapped to d. Regret defined via expected utility but stated with probability 1-delta. Proof is asymptotic (T -> infinity) and hides delta, ell, chi_u, B. Horizon labelled anytime since algorithm loop does not use T, but this is not explicitly stated.
